heard: March 2013, Bitcoin split into two chains.
said: March twenty thirteen. Bitcoin split into two chains.

heard: and the developers chose to kill the newer one.
said: And the developers chose to kill the newer one.

heard: It started with an update. Version 0.8 was brand new, but many computers still ran 0.7.
said: It started with an update. Version zero point eight was brand new, but many computers still ran zero point seven.

heard: Then, one huge block arrived.  It touched over 5,000 transactions.
said: Then one huge block arrived. It touched over five thousand transactions.

heard: The new computers accepted it. The old ones choked.
said: The new computers accepted it. The old ones choked.

heard: It needed over 10,000 database locks. The old version ran out.
said: It needed over ten thousand database locks. The old version ran out.

heard: Now there were two bitcoins at the same time.
said: Now there were two Bitcoins at the same time.

heard: Mount Gox and BitPay shut down deposits.
said: Mount Gox and BitPay shut down deposits.
And the price dropped twenty-four percent.

heard: So developers asked the big miners to go back to the old version.
said: So developers asked the big miners to go back to the old version.

heard: About six hours later, the old chain took the lead and won.
said: About six hours later, the old chain took the lead, and won.

said: And someone spent the same ten thousand dollars twice, against OKPay.
One block. Two Bitcoins. Bug, or warning?
